data.title: Pityriasis versicolor — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 7 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pityriasis versicolor** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. Causative organism?**
- Malassezia globosa (mainly), M. furfur, M. sympodialis — lipophilic yeasts of normal flora that convert to mycelial form

**Q2. Predisposing factors?**
- Hot humid climate, sweating, oily skin (adolescents/young adults), oily applications, pregnancy, Cushing/steroids, immunosuppression, malnutrition, genetic predisposition

**Q3. Clinical features?**
- Hypo- or hyperpigmented (or erythematous) round/oval macules with fine branny scale on upper trunk, neck, upper arms; 'evoked scale' (Besnier's sign/scratch sign) on stretching or scratching

**Q4. Why hypopigmentation?**
- Azelaic acid (dicarboxylic acid) produced by Malassezia inhibits tyrosinase; also pityriacitrin/malassezin effects and screening of UV

**Q5. Investigations?**
- KOH: short hyphae and round yeasts — 'spaghetti and meatballs'
- Wood's lamp: yellow-orange/golden fluorescence (not always)
- Scotch tape test, dermoscopy

**Q6. Differential diagnosis?**
- Vitiligo (no scale, chalky white), pityriasis alba, post-inflammatory hypopigmentation, leprosy (anaesthetic), seborrhoeic dermatitis, pityriasis rosea, confluent and reticulated papillomatosis, erythrasma, nevus depigmentosus

**Q7. Treatment?**
- Topical: ketoconazole 2% shampoo as body wash (5 min daily for 3 days), selenium sulfide 2.5%, zinc pyrithione, azole creams, terbinafine solution
- Systemic for extensive/recurrent: fluconazole 300 mg weekly × 2 (or 400 mg single), itraconazole 200 mg/day for 5–7 days (oral terbinafine and griseofulvin are ineffective)
- Prophylaxis: monthly shampoo/itraconazole 400 mg once monthly in hot months
- Pigment takes months to return — explain to patient

## Quick spotter facts
- Fine scaly hypopigmented macules on the upper back — pityriasis versicolor

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Superficial fungal infection — tinea versicolor); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.18. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
